title: Quasi-compact immersions of algebraic spaces are local on the base
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $h:Z\to T$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be an fppf covering. For algebraic spaces such a covering means a family whose pullback by each scheme mapping to $T$ is an fppf covering on etale scheme charts [def-pc-fppf-site]. Then $h$ is a quasi-compact immersion if and only if each $Z\times_TT_i\to T_i$ is a quasi-compact immersion. Here an immersion of algebraic spaces is representable by schemes and every scheme base change factors as a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]; quasi-compact means that pullback to a quasi-compact scheme has quasi-compact source [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. In particular the assertion includes descent of representability by schemes.

source.place: Tag 0424, lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact-immersion (fpqc locality, specialized to fppf coverings).

proof.text: Put $P(f)=$ quasi-compact immersion. The affine-test equivalences for immersions and quasi-compactness give hypothesis (2) of the fpqc property criterion and base-change stability. For hypothesis (1), take finitely many maps $f_j:X_j\to Y_j$ with $P$. Their sheaf coproducts are algebraic spaces. A scheme test $W\to\coprod_jY_j$ partitions $W$ into the clopen pieces $W_j$ pulling back $Y_j$; the pullback source over $W_j$ is $X_j\times_{Y_j}W_j$. The immersion criterion applied to this open cover makes the coproduct map an immersion. If $W$ is affine, each clopen $W_j$ is quasi-compact (closed in the quasi-compact space $W$), so each pullback source is quasi-compact, and their finite disjoint union is quasi-compact: choose finite subcovers on the pieces. The quasi-compact affine-test criterion now gives $P$ for the coproduct. For the empty family both source and target are empty, an isomorphism and quasi-compact. Coproducts and all charts are taken within the fixed size convention.

source.place: Tag 0424, first paragraph; Tag 041J (lemma-descending-properties-morphisms), hypotheses (1) and (2).

proof.text: Check hypothesis (3) of the criterion. Let $V\to U$ be flat surjective between affine schemes and $X\to U$ an algebraic-space morphism such that $X_V\to V$ is a quasi-compact immersion. Its source is a scheme by representability. The scheme factorization lemma writes $X_V\xrightarrow{j}C\xrightarrow{i}V$ with $j$ open and $i$ closed. Since $V$ is affine, $C$ is affine by the affine closed-immersion criterion. Also $X_V$ is quasi-compact: it is the inverse image of the quasi-compact open $V$ under the quasi-compact scheme map $X_V\to V$. Thus $j$ exhibits $X_V$ as a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme, which is precisely the quasi-affine hypothesis for the next step.

source.place: Tag 0424, sentence X prime to Z prime is quasi-affine; scheme argument of morphisms.tex Tag 02JR (lemma-quasi-compact-immersion-quasi-affine).

proof.text: Apply quasi-affine scheme representability descent to $V\to U$ and $X\to U$. The preceding step verifies its quasi-affine scheme source hypothesis upstairs, and the cover is flat surjective and affine-to-affine. Hence $X$ is a scheme. Now apply scheme quasi-compact-immersion descent to the same square. Its scheme-source hypothesis is now satisfied and its upstairs hypothesis is exactly the original assumption on $X_V\to V$. Consequently $X\to U$ is a quasi-compact immersion. This proves hypothesis (3), including the previously unassumed representability.

source.place: Tag 0424, last paragraph, using 0423 and 02L8. The phrase closed immersion in line 1745 is a typo; the required and obtained conclusion is quasi-compact immersion.

proof.text: The fpqc property criterion now applies to the isomorphism-invariant property $P$: step 1 supplies its finite-coproduct and affine-test hypotheses, and steps 2-3 supply its affine flat-surjective descent hypothesis. It yields $P(h)$ if and only if $P(h\times_TT_i)$ for every fpqc covering of $T$.

The given fppf covering is fpqc: on a scheme pullback, take the etale scheme charts specified in its covering convention and apply the scheme fppf-to-fpqc lemma. For each affine test these charts have finite flat affine refinements as in that lemma, with their maps into the original $T_i$; these are exactly the refinements required in the algebraic-space fpqc convention of the criterion. Thus step 4 applies to the given family. The forward implication also follows directly from the base-change clauses of the affine-test lemmas. If the covering is empty its target is empty, and the asserted immersion is the empty isomorphism.
